goal: I am a software developer. I need to modify the seat booking functionality to introduce new booking rules. Before making changes to the code, I need to understand the high-level architecture supporting this functionality. I want to identify the main components involved in the booking process, their responsibilities, and the interactions and dependencies among them. In particular, I need to understand which components are responsible for handling booking requests, checking seat availability, applying booking rules, managing and storing reservations, and interacting with external services such as the notification service. This understanding will help me identify which parts of the system need to be modified and which other components may be affected by the changes.

elements.name: ReservationController
responsibilities: REST boundary for create, cancel and check-in of reservations

elements.name: LibraryFacade
responsibilities: single entry point that delegates client requests to the managers

elements.name: ReservationManager
responsibilities: validates and creates reservations
handles cancel and check-in
applies the seat assignment strategy

elements.name: Area
responsibilities: computes the available seats for a date and time slot

elements.name: ReservationRegistry
responsibilities: stores and finds reservations through PersistenceManager

elements.name: FirstAvailableAssignment
responsibilities: assignment strategy that picks the first available seat

elements.name: PersistenceManager
responsibilities: saves, updates and queries JPA entities via EntityManager

elements.name: NotificationManager
responsibilities: builds notification messages and sends them to the notification service
sends reminders for reservations

fragments.guard: room null, inactive or closed on date -> IllegalArgumentException
area missing or not in room -> IllegalArgumentException
seatId != 0; seat missing or not in selected area -> IllegalArgumentException
inside synchronized block; true -> IllegalArgumentException (duplicate booking)
empty list -> IllegalArgumentException("No seats are available in the selected area")
seatId > 0 and seat not available -> IllegalStateException("The selected seat is no longer available")

limitations: one scenario per view; also recovered: cancel reservation, scheduled reminders, scheduled end-of-reservation handling
